page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.4-64 is a flexible compute instance powered by a 3.0 GHz Intel Xeon 6354 processor. The configuration allocates 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory. This yields an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation ratio, supported by hardware-level cryptographic acceleration such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, as well as AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address and features no bundled local storage, requiring remote block storage attachments for persistent state.

Benchmark results place the instance in the top 25% for memory subsystem performance, recording a PassMark memory score of 2765.68 alongside an uncached read bandwidth of 62.05 GB/s and write bandwidth of 42.84 GB/s. Standard computing scores fall within the mid-range tier, showing a single-core Geekbench score of 1699.0 and a multi-core score of 6336.0, complemented by a multi-core stress-ng rating of 7927.96. Static web serving throughput reaches 14.61 GB/s, while in-memory operations register 8.1 million Redis SET operations per second.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio and robust memory subsystem deliver solid resource efficiency for memory-bound workloads, though absence of integrated NVMe storage requires balancing remote network storage throughput against transactional IOPS requirements. Natural language processing benchmarks illustrate that medium-scale LLM inference (7B model at 7.62 tokens per second) is heavily constrained on this x86 CPU footprint. The configuration is primarily tailored for in-memory caching layers, medium databases, Clang compilation jobs, and high-throughput web service stacks.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.4-64 is a compute instance configured with 4 dedicated physical cores (8 vCPUs) on an Intel Xeon 6354 processor running at 3.0 GHz, complemented by 64.0 GB of RAM. Featuring an x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic instructions, it provides an elevated 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. In synthetic testing, the instance exhibits top-quartile memory performance with a PassMark memory score of 2765.68, alongside average CPU compute throughput reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 6336.0 and 8.1 million Redis SET operations per second. The server includes one public IPv4 address and lacks integrated local storage, directing persistent data to attached network volumes. Without hardware accelerators, it is unsuited for heavy deep learning inference, but it delivers balanced, cost-effective capacity for in-memory caches, backend compilation tasks, enterprise application middleware, and relational databases.
